verdict.rationale: Alloy documents first-party outbound webhooks for asynchronous events such as watchlist updates and manual reviews. Deliveries are signed with a shared secret, retried on exponential backoff for 24 hours, and automatically disabled after repeated failures, with webhook settings to re-enable them. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the subscription/registration steps and per-event-type selection, a full catalog of webhook event types, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: They're particularly useful for Journeys and asynchronous events like when a watchlist gets updated or a manual review occurs.
Alloy signs the request body with a shared secret and sends the signature in the Authorization header
retries continue on an exponential backoff for a duration of 24 hours from the time of the first failure.
You can re-enable it by setting to active in your webhook settings.
